chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim ibn 'Uthman, from Abu 'Ubaydah al-Hadda', who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'Any dhimmi (non-Muslim subject) who buys land from a Muslim, then khums is due upon him.'

key_terms.أَبَا جَعْفَرٍ: Abu Ja'far (Imam al-Baqir), peace be upon him
key_terms.ذِمِّيٍّ: Dhimmi, a non-Muslim subject living under Islamic rule

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on khums for a dhimmi buying land from a Muslim?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies that the obligation of khums extends to real estate acquisitions by dhimmis (non-Muslim subjects) from Muslims, a ruling attributed to Imam al-Sadiq. It underscores the fiscal integration of non-Muslims into the Islamic economic system, distinguishing this transactional khums from the khums on war booty. This specific application highlights the Imamate's authority in defining financial liabilities across different demographic groups within the Islamic state.
